examples.text: 아니 입수를 안 하면 뭘 하겠다는 거야?
examples.trans: Wait, if she won't go into the water, what is she going to do on the show?
I bought bread. And I bought milk too.
Let's eat and then depart.

meanings.note: Combines 시청 ('watching and listening') + 자 ('person').

examples.trans: Many viewers like that drama.
We listened carefully to viewer feedback.

examples.text: 역사를 더듬어 보자면, 주로 침체기에 썼던 카드가 입수, 그리고 시청자 투어입니다!
examples.trans: Tracing the show's history, the classic trump cards during slumps were cold-water plunges and the Viewer Tour!

examples.text: 한 시간 내내 입수만 하니? 시청자 투어 옛날에 대박 났지, 사십 퍼센트씩 나오고! 우리 여태 한 거 다 합쳐도 안 나오는데 뭘.
examples.trans: Are we going to jump in water for a whole hour? Sure, the Viewer Tour hit forty percent back then—all our episodes combined barely add up to that!

meanings.note: Determiner form of 하나, used before a noun counter.

examples.trans: one person
one hour

meanings.note: Available time or duration.
Used with native Korean numbers to count hours (한 시간 = one hour).

examples.trans: Do you have time?
It takes two hours.

examples.text: 한 시간 내내 입수만 하니? 시청자 투어 옛날에 대박 났지, 사십 퍼센트씩 나오고! 우리 여태 한 거 다 합쳐도 안 나오는데 뭘.
examples.trans: Are we going to jump in water for a whole hour? Sure, the Viewer Tour hit forty percent back then—all our episodes combined barely add up to that!

examples.text: 내내 준비하면 좋은 결과가 나올 거예요.
examples.trans: If we prepare (throughout, all along), good results will follow.

meanings.en: the old days, old times, the past

examples.trans: In the old days, this neighborhood was quiet.
Sometimes I think of the old days.

examples.text: 한 시간 내내 입수만 하니? 시청자 투어 옛날에 대박 났지, 사십 퍼센트씩 나오고! 우리 여태 한 거 다 합쳐도 안 나오는데 뭘.
examples.trans: Are we going to jump in water for a whole hour? Sure, the Viewer Tour hit forty percent back then—all our episodes combined barely add up to that!

examples.text: 저한테는 선배님이 사십 퍼센트 같습니다. 전 시즌 시청률 다 합쳐도 도달할 수 없는, 아무리 노력해도 얻을 수 없는 꿈의 시청률 같습니다, 진심으로.
examples.trans: To me, Senior Ye-jin feels like forty percent—a dream rating out of reach no matter how hard I try, even adding every episode together.

meanings.note: Used as percentage + -로 (85%로).

examples.trans: So far, "it was intentional" is winning overwhelmingly at eighty-five percent.
This point about at eighty-five percent is really important.

meanings.note: dummy

examples.trans: dummy trans 1
dummy trans 2

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.
I understand well (still, until now).
Today is a (still, until now) busy day.

examples.text: 한 시간 내내 입수만 하니? 시청자 투어 옛날에 대박 났지, 사십 퍼센트씩 나오고! 우리 여태 한 거 다 합쳐도 안 나오는데 뭘.
examples.trans: Are we going to jump in water for a whole hour? Sure, the Viewer Tour hit forty percent back then—all our episodes combined barely add up to that!

examples.text: 저한테는 선배님이 사십 퍼센트 같습니다. 전 시즌 시청률 다 합쳐도 도달할 수 없는, 아무리 노력해도 얻을 수 없는 꿈의 시청률 같습니다, 진심으로.
examples.trans: To me, Senior Ye-jin feels like forty percent—a dream rating out of reach no matter how hard I try, even adding every episode together.

meanings.note: colloquial contraction of 무엇; also used rhetorically to brush off a question

examples.trans: What are you doing now?
Why are you even asking something like that?

meanings.note: Introduces a contrast, unexpected turn, or new topic. In everyday speech it is very often contracted to 근데. RR: geureonde; spoken geunde.

examples.trans: I contacted them. But there is no reply.
By the way, what time is it now?

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그것

examples.trans: Where did you buy that?
That is a really good idea.

examples.text: 웃겨? 야, 넌 남자 아니냐? 내일 촬영 준비나 해.
examples.trans: Funny, aren't you a man too? Go get ready for tomorrow's shoot.
The topic of preparation came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Used to count the number of months.

examples.trans: three months
three months (2)

meanings.note: Used colloquially for positive or negative emphasis.
Original sense of exceeding a limit.

examples.trans: The weather is so nice today.
Don't worry too much.
Did you hear about this owner?
I was busy today because of owner.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: Even if I put myself in that female celebrity's shoes…
Here the word for 'even in the position of' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 잘 생각해보세요, 저런 여자가 의외로 진국일 수가 있다니까.
examples.trans: Give it serious thought—a woman like her can turn out to be the real deal.
This expression comes from 'think it over'.

examples.text: 뭘 어떻게 해야 할지 모르겠으면 아무것도 안 하면 돼요.
examples.trans: If you don't know what to do, you don't have to do anything at all.
The topic of anything at all came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: used to emphasize an adjective or adverb

examples.trans: The food is really delicious today.
Time really flies.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 좀 애매한 건데 어떻게 네가 좀 알아볼 수 있겠니?
examples.trans: It is a bit borderline—could you find out for me somehow?
This expression comes from 'ambiguous, borderline'.

examples.text: 근데 그 음식점 주인 입장에서 생각해보면 아무것도 안 하고 있기도 참 애매한 거라, 단골들만 데리고 있다가는 임대료 못 내고 장사 접게 생겼으니까.
examples.trans: Still, from that restaurant owner's shoes, sitting still feels impossible too—when keeping only a handful of regulars cannot even pay the rent.
The topic of only regular customers came up in today's meeting.

examples.text: 우리 애 데려다가 이게 웬 망신이야?
examples.trans: Bringing my star out here only to embarrass her like this?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 데리다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (bringing along and).

examples.text: 근데 그 음식점 주인 입장에서 생각해보면 아무것도 안 하고 있기도 참 애매한 거라, 단골들만 데리고 있다가는 임대료 못 내고 장사 접게 생겼으니까.
examples.trans: Still, from that restaurant owner's shoes, sitting still feels impossible too—when keeping only a handful of regulars cannot even pay the rent.
The topic of rent came up in today's meeting.

meanings.note: Placed before a verb to express inability or impossibility.

examples.text: 어제는 너무 피곤해서 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.trans: I was so tired yesterday that I couldn't sleep.
Because it rained, we couldn't go on the picnic.

examples.text: 지는 티 안 내려고 무지 애쓰는데 원래 티가 나는 거예요.
examples.trans: He tries hard not to let it show, but feelings like that always show.

examples.text: 티 안 내려고 무지 애는 쓰시는데 저는 조금 알 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: She tries hard not to show it, yet I think I understand that feeling a little.

examples.text: 근데 그 음식점 주인 입장에서 생각해보면 아무것도 안 하고 있기도 참 애매한 거라, 단골들만 데리고 있다가는 임대료 못 내고 장사 접게 생겼으니까.
examples.trans: Still, from that restaurant owner's shoes, sitting still feels impossible too—when keeping only a handful of regulars cannot even pay the rent.
The topic of business, shop came up in today's meeting.

접다.gloss: to fold, to wrap up, to shut down

meanings.en: to wrap up, to shut down, to give up (a project or business)
meanings.note: Colloquial/figurative sense.

examples.trans: Fold the paper in half.
Let's just scrap this project.

meanings.note: Used for time or order.

examples.trans: Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.
